does: For one character view model: finds the character's last active interactive dialogue instance (LSDialogs::DialogManager::GetLastActiveInteractiveInstanceFor), and when the provider has its game data (+8) and the view model has its player properties (+0x420) sets that dialogue as the active one (gui::VMPlayerCharacterProperties::SetActiveDialogue).

evidence.says: The decompiled body: the instance lookup, the two null checks, GetDialogueFromInstanceId and SetActiveDialogue.

Probed during a dialogue's start: natively called for the talker (+0x420 null) and the host (+0x420 set) and SetActiveDialogue runs; with nothing drawn from the process start both have +0x420 null and the dialogue window stays empty.
